newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/OEX off to slow start, awaits FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/OEX off to slow start, awaits FOMC.

text.p: U.S. stock index options were off to a slow start on Monday in typical post-expiration trade after Friday's May options settlement, traders said.
Caution ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting also subdued activity and kept implied volatility levels hovering at relatively high levels, they added.

"You've got the Fed meeting tomorrow, so there's going to be hesitation," said Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co. "I don't think they (stocks) are going to do much on the upside today."
None of the front-month June contracts in the S&P 100 index options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) had volume of more than 1,500 contracts by 1040 CDT/1540 GMT.
The OEX was up 1.51 point to 814.07 at 1040 CDT/1540 GMT.

The CBOE volatility index .VIX, which reflects implied volatilities for near-month OEX options, was off 0.14 point at 24.07. The VIX has been fluctuating between 20 and 25 for most of the year after drifting in the high teens through most of 1996 and in the low teens in 1995.
Traders said volatilities might spike up if the Federal Reserve raised interest rates on Tuesday, but they said volatilities should eventually come back down toward 20 again.
"If there's a hike you might see a pop in volatility initially, but I think you're going to see it come in," said a market maker on the CBOE floor.

"If they raise rates only as expected (25 basis points), you might see a relief rally that there won't be any further hikes in the near future," he said, adding that a Fed decision not to raise rates would probably draw the same response.
Shartsis said April's heavy put buying, a positive signal for contrarians, was still having a lasting effect.

"In April we had a very intense, extended period of put buying," he said. "Usually, you're going to get more than a month (of bullishness) out of that. If you accept the idea that you'll get a few months out of that, any setback here should be a buying opportunity."
A recent rise in open interest in put options on Treasury bond futures might also provide a cushion against market turmoil in the event of a credit tightening, he said.

Tim Ord, publisher of Ord Oracle, said he saw a wedge pattern in intraday charts that could lead to a pullback in the OEX toward 795 and that candlesticks in the latter half of last week were also bearish.
Still, he noted that wedge patterns generally signaled a short-term pause of a trend and were not a long-term topping formation.
"There's going to be a shakeout to the downside coming into that trendline (drawn from mid-April lows) and then we go up and break new highs," Ord predicted.
